prompt: Design a production operating model for multi-rack OpenStack with OVN/OVS: tenant east-west, distributed routing, centralized north-south gateways, ACL/security groups, NAT, load balancing, provider VLANs and Geneve. Define ownership, failure domains, capacity, security, observability, incident response, upgrade/rollback and recovery acceptance.
directAnswer: Map each owner: CMS intent, NB desired state, northd compilation, SB flows/bindings, chassis controller translation, local OVSDB configuration, OpenFlow policy, datapath cache, Linux/NIC/underlay transport and workload/user outcome. Cluster NB/SB across independent failures and measure quorum plus commit progress. Measure northd/controller generation lag. Standardize chassis identity, encap endpoints, bridge mappings, VLANs, ofports and MTU. Version policy inputs and schema/protocol contracts. Capacity-plan state/update rates, compile/recompute latency, flows/masks/upcalls/conntrack, tunnels, gateways, CPU/memory/bandwidth and largest-failure reserve. Protect database/OpenFlow channels, certificates, sockets, RBAC, logs and captures. Alert on user symptoms and sustained convergence or transport risk. Canary one failure domain with old/new bidirectional application flows. Accept recovery only after authoritative state, correct policy/NAT, observed delivery/reply, stable SLI and exact cleanup.
foundation: Control-plane availability, convergence and forwarding are separate. Capacity is multidimensional and recovery becomes unsafe when stale bindings, duplicate gateways, broad flow mutation or ambiguous ownership exists.

seniorAnswer: I would require stable identities and progress markers at every handoff. NB/SB quorum, northd and controller convergence, OVS/OpenFlow realization, physical transport and user results get separate objectives. Capacity covers state/update rate, compile time, flows/masks/upcalls/conntrack, gateway and underlay throughput, and survivor reserve. Changes canary one domain and stop on convergence or SLI regression. Recovery requires correct authoritative state, policy/NAT, observed bidirectional application behavior and residue removal.
